title: Fortresses
description: Positions where the weaker side cannot be broken down. Four set-ups worth knowing by sight, because they save lost-looking games.
source: Every position is dealt fresh and judged by Lichess's endgame tablebase, which is perfect for seven pieces or fewer. These drills need a connection.

drills.name: The wrong-coloured bishop
drills.goal: They have a bishop and a rook pawn, but the bishop does not control the queening corner. Draw it.
drills.idea: If the bishop cannot attack the corner square, a king sitting there can never be driven out.
method: Run for the corner the pawn is heading to.
Take the shortest path. Going after the pawn wastes the move you need.
Once there, shuffle between the corner and the square beside it.
They can only stalemate you or give the pawn away.

drills.name: Opposite-coloured bishops
drills.goal: Two pawns down with bishops of opposite colours. Set up the blockade and hold it.
drills.idea: Your bishop and king control squares their bishop can never contest. Two extra pawns are not enough if they cannot both advance.
method: Put your king in front of the pawns, on a square their bishop cannot attack.
Put your bishop where it attacks a pawn, so their king is tied to defending it.
Keep the bishop on the diagonal that stops the pawns stepping forward together.
Then wait, moving the bishop up and down that diagonal.

drills.name: Knight against a rook pawn
drills.goal: A lone knight against a rook pawn and its king. Stop the pawn.
drills.idea: A knight in front of a rook pawn holds it by itself, as long as the pawn has not reached the seventh.
method: Get the knight to the square in front of the pawn, or to one that covers its next step.
Use forks: a check that also covers the queening square gains a move.
On its post, the knight hops between the squares that keep the pawn stopped.
Bring your king over only if it does not cost the knight its post.

drills.name: Bishop against a rook
drills.goal: A bishop against a rook, with your king near a corner. Find the safe corner and hold.
drills.idea: In the corner your bishop does not control, the bishop can always block a check on the edge and any tighter squeeze is stalemate.
method: Head for a corner square of the colour your bishop does not travel on.
Keep the bishop close enough to block a check along the edge.
When the rook pins the bishop against your king, they have no follow-up: a waiting move by them is stalemate.
Stay out of the corner your bishop does control. There the same idea loses.

drills.name: Random position
drills.goal: One of the drills above, and you are not told which. Work out what the position is worth first.
drills.idea: Read the position before you move: what is the material, where are the kings, and which method does it call for?
method: Name the position type before touching a piece.
